$comment: Every module that builds an LLM prompt, next to WHO WROTE the text it renders. Read on every build by test-unit/untrusted-surface-census.test.mjs, inside `npm run test:unit` → `npm run check:ci` → .husky/pre-push.
$why: The adversarial corpus next door proves that the surfaces somebody THOUGHT of are quarantined. It cannot say anything about the ones nobody did — and that is the failure this repository actually had: `onboarding-scan` pasted the text of a website into a prompt (a site an anonymous visitor picks, through the public /sken mode), `local-page` pasted public review bodies into a prompt whose output is PUBLISHED, and `channel-research` grounded on profile prose the scan had derived from that same page text. Three unfenced third-party surfaces, none of them noticed by a green build, because nothing had ever enumerated the question. A census is what turns 'we quarantined the ones we remembered' into 'every builder has an answer on file'.
$howToChange: Adding a tool means adding its row. If the row says `outside`, the module has to actually quarantine (src/lib/ai/untrusted.ts) and the corpus has to exercise one of its builders — the test refuses the row otherwise, so the declaration cannot be the cheap way out. If it says `tenant` or `none`, the `why` is the whole content of the row: name the fields and say where they come from, because that sentence is what a later reader checks against the code. Never move a row from `outside` to `tenant` to go green; the disagreement is the finding.

$origins.outside: renders text whose author is not the tenant — an ad account synced from Google Ads or Sklik, a public review, an inbound message from a stranger, a page fetched from a website, or profile prose derived from one of those.
$origins.tenant: renders only text the tenant typed into this app, or text this app computed from the tenant's own account (numbers, labels, derived rollups). The tenant steering their own prompt is not a privilege boundary.
$origins.none: renders no request text into a prompt at all — a fragment helper, a registry, or the provider adapter that transports a prompt somebody else built.

$cannotSee: WHETHER A CLASSIFICATION IS TRUE. This is a declaration, and the test holds it to the tree only where the tree can answer: an `outside` row must really quarantine, an exercised builder must really be exported, a named field must really appear in the module. A row that calls an outside field `tenant` is a wrong sentence, and the only thing that catches it is a reader — which is why the `why` names the fields rather than gesturing at them.

THE ROUTE. A field is classified by where its text comes FROM, not by which door it entered. `channel-research` is `outside` because its grounding is scan-derived even though a signed-in tenant triggers the call.

THE OUTPUT SIDE. Containment on the way in is one rung of three (src/lib/ai/untrusted.ts); an id the request never supplied being dropped and an out-of-vocabulary enum being coerced are the other two, and they live in each tool's normalizer.
